thread:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: prod-us-east-1 - model-warmup OOM detected on shard pool cluster-7. Severity: potential customer impact. Pager routed to @jessica and @eng-aaron :rotating_light:

jessica: got the pager, jumping in. seeing lots of warmup failures when we spin up rwd-13B-v2. errors look like OOM during load and a bunch of CUDA driver complaints.

eng-aaron: on my way. any immediate customer-facing errors?

jessica: early metrics: ~22k warmup attempts, ~1.6k failures in last 5m. 5xx rate for affected models up ~3.8%. seems concentrated on nodes with NVidia A100-80GB, but some smaller GPUs also hit.

sre-liz: logs from one of the failing pods:
```
[2026-03-15T09:12:34Z] warmup: load artifact 0x7ffa failed: deser error checksum mismatch
[2026-03-15T09:12:35Z] cuda: cuInit returned 35 (CUDA_ERROR_NO_DEVICE)
[2026-03-15T09:12:35Z] runtime: OOM while allocating 38GB for weights
```

mike: hmm checksum mismatch implies artifact corruption or network read issues from storage backend.

infra-bot: ALERT: node-flap detected: node-7c2 experienced kernel OOM messages and container restarts x4 in 3m.

eng-aaron: can we repro with the same artifact on a different node? if it's a storage read glitch we should see checksum mismatch reproducible.

jessica: tried pulling the artifact to a clean node, same deserialization fails. stacktrace indicates protobuf decode error during tensor layout read.

sre-liz: also seeing compile timeouts in the compile cache step (nvrtc kernels). one line:
```
compile: kernel_id=0x3a timeout=60s status=TIMED_OUT
```

eng-aaron: two orthogonal issues: (1) artifact deserialization checksum mismatch -> artifact corruption, (2) compile timeouts and OOM during warmup -> could be memory fragmentation or driver regression.

jessica: immediate mitigation idea: disable warmup-prefetch for the rwd-13B-v2 route and let steady-state serving rely on existing cached instances. fallback routes to smaller quantized variant rwd-13B-q4 if warmup fails.

customer-ops: any customers impacted yet? ops team reporting two customers (acme-analytics, finlytics) opened support tickets with increased 5xx.

mike: recommend temporarily routing new requests to rwd-7B-quant variant and scaling up dedicated pool in us-east-1 if possible. also mark rwd-13B-v2 as NO_WARMUP until we triage.

jessica: executing mitigation: set model config rwd-13B-v2.warmup.enabled=false -> pushing now.

oncall-bot: CONFIG CHANGE: rwd-13B-v2.warmup.enabled=false deployed at 09:20 UTC by jessica.

eng-aaron: kicked off artifact integrity audit for the affected artifact id: art-20260315-7b2. checksum mismatches across 3 storage nodes.

sre-liz: in parallel, increasing compile timeout from 60s -> 180s on compile cache to see if NVRTC transient spikes are causing failures. patching runtime flags.

infra-bot: scaling action: added 8 nodes to dedicated-pool-us-east-1 to absorb traffic to quantized variants.

jessica: after disabling warmup and routing, 5xxs dropped from 3.8% -> 0.6% within 3m. still monitoring for residual errors. notifying SOC and CSMs.

customer-ops: CSMs notified, proactively emailed top 10 affected customers. preparing incident banner if this escalates.

eng-aaron: next steps: (1) find root cause of artifact checksum failures — storage network path + object replication check. (2) validate kernel regressions with recent driver patch rolled last week. (3) postmortem owner assigned.

jessica: assigning postmortem -> eng-aaron (owner), sre-liz (on-call co-owner). severity downgraded to Sev3; still track until artifact and driver issues resolved.

mike: quick note: we should add a safeguard to block auto-warmup for artifacts with missing or failed checksum verification. small follow-up PR coming from eng.

jessica: thanks all. I'll leave this thread open while we watch for replays and confirm artifact fixes. if anyone sees a spike revert, ping immediately.

eng-aaron: pulling logs and will share a summary in #eng-runtime after analysis. thanks.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied. customer-impact: partial for 2 customers (recovered). next update scheduled in 30m or on significant change. :white_check_mark:
